                    ### Question
                    The intestinal absorption of iron is more effective:

                    ### Options
                    opa. In the form of ferric ion.
opb. In the form of heme group.
opc. Via the transferrin membrane transporter.
opd. If there are oxalates in digestive light.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Iron in the form of heme group is more effectively absorbed in the intestines compared to ferric ion. Absorption via the transferrin membrane transporter facilitates efficient uptake of iron into cells. The presence of oxalates in the digestive tract can bind to iron and inhibit absorption, reducing its effectiveness.
